top_signals.title: Fed’s Hammack Prefers Smaller, Frequent Rate Adjustments
top_signals.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack pointed to smaller, more frequent policy adjustments to help inflation expectations remain anchored. At an event in Cleveland Monday, Hammack stopped short of backing a rate increase this month, but said, “When feasible, I generally think it’s preferable to make smaller adjustments, and to do so relatively quickly, rather than to wait and risk needing a larger course correction.” (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations impacting rate path, bonds and global risk assets.

top_signals.title: LVMH Sales at Key Unit Tumble on Weaker Demand in China
top_signals.summary: Sales at LVMH’s biggest division slumped as worsening economic conditions and a consumer backlash in China hit its key Louis Vuitton brand.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: The diesel crisis is testing the limits of globalisation
top_signals.summary: Seemingly rational choices by individual states will weaken collective energy security and accelerate fragmentation
